title: Tenant-scoped control-plane VPC binding + DNS convergence workflow
author: Ayesha Raman
release_notes: Adds tenant-scoped control-plane VPC binding, conditional cross-account peering acceptance, zonal endpoint routing and a DNS convergence workflow for Private deployments. Includes Terraform module bump, Helm chart values and safe rollout hooks. No API changes.
description: Summary: Add tenant-scoped control-plane VPC binding so each Private deployment can pin the control-plane to a tenant-owned VPC/route domain and ensure deterministic egress/DNS behavior. This change wires together a Terraform module (vpc-binding) with the private-installer Helm hooks and adds a DNS convergence operator used during staged upgrades. Motivation: customers with multiple tenant VPCs reported intermittent control-plane DNS split-brain during upgrades and cross-account peering handoff. This PR: 1) introduces a tenant_vpc_binding Terraform module that creates/subscribes to: subnet allocations (zonal affinity), interface endpoints (control-plane privatelink), and least-privilege security groups; 2) implements an automated peering acceptance Lambda + IAM role template used for cross-account peering where the control-plane account needs to accept peering requests on behalf of tenants; 3) new installer Helm values to enable staged DNS convergence (dnsConvergence: true/false) and a preflight hook that validates prefixlists and route priorities; 4) safe upgrade/rollback hooks in the installer to atomically flip DNS forwarding and validate control-plane health before decommissioning old endpoints. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module vpc-binding with outputs for subnet claims, endpoint ARNs and SG IDs - [x] Helm chart changes: values schema, preflight hook, post-upgrade convergence job - [x] Installer change: staged rollout with canary tenant list and rollback sentinel - [x] Integration tests for peering acceptance and DNS convergence (local e2e harness) - [x] Update docs/installer/upgrade.md and add an operations runbook for rollback How it works (high level): - On install/upgrade with tenant_vpc_binding enabled the installer claims zonal subnets per tenant and creates private interface endpoints for the control-plane services. - A short-lived peering request is initiated from the tenant account; the peering-acceptor Lambda (deployed in control-plane account) validates the request using the new IAM role template and accepts on a per-tenant allowlist. - DNS convergence job waits for expected endpoint ARNs, then creates conditional forwarding rules (Route53 Resolver or Cloud DNS equivalents) and validates name resolution end-to-end. If validation fails, rollback sentinel is activated and the installer re-routes traffic to previous endpoints. Terraform/Helm/Installer changes (high level): - terraform/modules/vpc-binding/: new module with variables (tenant_id, zonal_subnet_map, privatelink_services, peering_policy) and outputs (subnet_claims, endpoint_arns, sg_ids) - terraform/examples/tenant-binding/ : example usage and cross-account role trust - charts/private-installer/values.schema.json : new dnsConvergence and peeringOptions blocks - charts/private-installer/templates/preflight-job.yaml : validates prefix lists and existing forwarders - charts/private-installer/templates/dns-converger-job.yaml : runs convergence/validation and writes status to a ConfigMap - pkg/installer/rollout.go : staged rollout controller that reads canary-tenants and safety-sentinels - docs/installer/upgrade.md : added section "Tenant VPC binding and DNS convergence" Testing performed: - Unit tests for Terraform module via terraform validate and module-level plan diffs - Local e2e harness runs that simulate cross-account peering and DNS resolution across 3 AZs; initial run exposed a race where conditional forwarders were created before endpoint propagation; fixed by adding a short polling backoff and idempotent endpoint existence checks - CI: lint/validate/build/helm-template/render all passed; e2e pipeline was flaky on first run due to mock IAM token expiry, re-run succeeded. Rollout plan: - Ship behind feature flag (dnsConvergence=false default) - Enable on a small set of internal tenants as canary and run convergence job in dry-run mode - After 72h of stable metrics (error budget, DNS resolution latency), flip live traffic and enable peering automation for the tenant - Monitor metrics: control_plane_dns_errors, endpoint_failover_count, peering_accept_errors - If convergence job fails, the installer will automatically revert forwarding entries and mark the release as rollback-needed Backward compatibility and upgrade notes: - Default behavior unchanged unless dnsConvergence is explicitly enabled in Helm values - Operators upgrading older installers will get a migration job that only runs when tenant_vpc_binding is set true - The module exposes clear outputs so downstream orgs can opt into manual peering acceptance instead of the automated Lambda Security considerations: - Created least-privilege IAM trust document for the peering-acceptor and ensured SG rules only allow necessary control-plane ports between endpoints - Secrets (KMS keys) used by the converger job are optional and must be provided by the operator in values.secretReferences Review summary: - Major design reviewed by Marco Li (networking) and Priya Suresh (security) - Janelle requested tightening of prefixlist checks and an explicit timeout for the convergence job; addressed in second commit - Two follow-up TODOs captured in ENG-1248 for metrics and improved observability

notes_for_ops: Operators must supply tenant account role ARNs if they do not want automated peering acceptance. When enabling dnsConvergence, run the provided dry-run job and watch control_plane_dns_errors metric. Rollback is automatic on convergence validation failure.
